title: How do you build a training matrix for a pharmacy?
description: Build a pharmacy training matrix: pharmacist CE and CPD cycles, mandatory topics, privacy, chemical safety and reporting duties, with a worked example.
shortAnswer: A pharmacy training matrix is built in two layers. The first tracks each pharmacist's personal licensure cycle, such as 30 hours every two years in California, Florida and Texas or 40 CPD credits a year in Australia, including the state mandated topics. The second covers workplace duties the pharmacy itself owns, such as HIPAA privacy and security training, hazard communication and child abuse reporting, with a frequency and an evidence rule for each.
keyTakeaways: Pharmacist continuing education belongs to the licensee, but the pharmacy still needs it in the matrix because an unrenewed license takes a pharmacist off the roster.

Hours are not the whole duty: California, Florida and Texas each require specific topics, such as law, controlled substances, medication errors, cultural competency or human trafficking, inside the 30 hours.
Australia counts credits rather than hours: at least 40 a year to 30 September, at least 20 from Group 2 or Group 3 activities, with no pro rata reduction for part-time pharmacists.
Workplace rows carry their own clocks: HIPAA privacy training at onboarding and after material policy changes, and hazard communication training at initial assignment and when new hazards appear.
As at November 2026, the hazard communication deadline of November 20, 2026 and the Ahpra review of CPD standards are the changes most likely to alter pharmacy rows.

sections.heading: What makes a pharmacy training matrix different?

blocks.text: A pharmacy's most demanding training duties sit with individual licensees, not with the business, so the matrix has to track obligations the pharmacy does not own but cannot operate without. Every pharmacist on the roster carries a renewal cycle set by a state board or national board, while the pharmacy carries privacy, chemical safety and reporting duties for its whole workforce.

The approach in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) applies unchanged: people down one axis, obligations across the other, a rule in each cell. What a pharmacy adds is an ownership column, showing whether a cell is the pharmacist's licensure duty or the employer's workplace duty, and a unit column, because hours, contact hours and credits do not convert cleanly. Hospital pharmacy departments should also check the [hospital training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix-for-a-hospital) for rows they inherit from the wider facility.

sections.heading: Which obligations apply to pharmacies in each market?

blocks.text: Take the columns from the regulation pages for every jurisdiction where the pharmacy holds a license or employs pharmacists. Each summary uses only facts recorded on the linked page.

items: **California.** 16 CCR 1732.5 requires 30 hours in the prior 24 months, including 2 hours of board provided law and ethics and 1 hour of cultural competency. Pharmacists who provide specialized services need further hours, such as 1 for smoking cessation, 2 for travel medicine, 1 for emergency contraception and 1 for immunization, and Schedule II prescribers need 1 hour every four years ([pharmacist CE in the US](/regulations/pharmacist-continuing-education-requirements-us)).

**Florida.** Section 465.009 requires not less than 30 hours in two years, including a 3 hour vaccine and epinephrine course. The Board of Pharmacy splits the hours into 26 general, 2 on controlled substances and 2 on medication errors, and section 456.0341 required a 1 hour human trafficking course by January 1, 2021 ([human trafficking training](/regulations/human-trafficking-training-requirements-healthcare)).

**Texas.** 22 TAC 295.8 requires 30 contact hours per license period, including 1 hour of Texas law, 2 hours on controlled substance prescribing and monitoring by the first anniversary, and the human trafficking prevention course required by Occupations Code 116.002.

**United States, federal.** 45 CFR 164.530(b) requires HIPAA privacy training for all workforce members, new members within a reasonable period and after material policy changes, documented and kept six years; 164.308(a)(5) requires a security awareness and training program for all workforce members including management ([HIPAA training](/regulations/hipaa-security-and-privacy-training)). 29 CFR 1910.1200(h) requires hazard communication training at initial assignment and whenever a new chemical hazard is introduced ([hazard communication](/regulations/osha-hazard-communication-training-requirements)). Where a pharmacist's duties create occupational exposure to blood, 29 CFR 1910.1030 requires training at initial assignment and at least annually ([bloodborne pathogens](/regulations/osha-bloodborne-pathogens-training-requirements)).

**Australia.** The Pharmacy Board of Australia's CPD registration standard requires annual CPD planning and at least 40 credits in each 12 month period ending 30 September, at least 20 from Group 2 or Group 3 ([pharmacist CPD in Australia](/regulations/pharmacist-cpd-requirements-australia)). Section 128 of the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law makes CPD a registration duty, and breach can lead to health, conduct or performance action ([Ahpra CPD standards](/regulations/ahpra-cpd-registration-standards)). In South Australia, pharmacists are prescribed health practitioners under section 30(5) of the Children and Young People (Safety) Act 2017 and must report suspected risk to a child ([mandatory reporting](/regulations/mandatory-reporting-training-australia)). The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner names regular staff training as a reasonable step under APP 1 and APP 11 ([Privacy Act training](/regulations/privacy-act-staff-training-requirements)).

blocks.text: For US providers, the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE) defines 60 minutes of live credit as 1 contact hour, or 0.1 CEU, and requires providers to upload credit to CPE Monitor within 60 days. The matrix can therefore treat the CPE Monitor e-profile as the official source rather than collecting paper certificates.

sections.heading: Which pharmacy cycles are fixed and which are chosen?

blocks.text: Licensure cycles are fixed by the boards, while most workplace cycles are left to the pharmacy. Mark the source of each interval so that a reviewer can tell a board rule from a business choice.

items: **Fixed by the board.** Two year, 30 hour cycles in California and Florida, a 30 contact hour license period in Texas, and an annual 40 credit period in Australia that runs 1 October to 30 September, with renewal due 30 November.

**No flexibility in Australia.** The Board allows no pro rata or part-time reduction, no rollover of surplus credits and no exemption granted in advance. Absence of one to three years requires a year's CPD quota before recommencing.
**Event driven.** HIPAA privacy training follows a material change in policies, and hazard communication training follows the introduction of a new chemical hazard.

**Chosen by the pharmacy.** Neither HIPAA rule currently sets an annual frequency, and the annual privacy training duty in the Australian Government Agencies APP Code applies to agencies, not to private pharmacies. Record the reason for the chosen cycle, using [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) as a method.

sections.heading: What evidence do boards and regulators ask pharmacies for?

blocks.text: Boards audit individual pharmacists, and federal and state agencies examine the pharmacy, so the matrix needs evidence for both. Keep licensure evidence linked to the person and workplace evidence linked to the site.

items: **Board audits.** The Texas rule provides for audit and discipline, and nonrenewal for failure to report. The Pharmacy Board of Australia runs random audits through the year, and its guidelines list nine record fields required at audit.
**Official records.** ACPE treats the CPE Monitor e-profile as the official record of ACPE credit for US pharmacists.
**Workplace records.** HIPAA documentation is kept six years from creation or last effective date. Hazard communication training content must cover the elements in 1910.1200(h)(2) and (h)(3).

**Quality of activities.** The Australian guidelines say sponsor driven product detailing is unlikely to be of sufficient quality, so in-house sessions should be designed to count. See [evidencing training effectiveness to a regulator](/guides/how-to-evidence-training-effectiveness-to-a-regulator).

sections.heading: Which pharmacy rule changes fall in 2026 and 2027?

blocks.text: Enter the following as dated rows so that affected cells update on the right day. As at November 2026, the regulation pages record:

items: **January 2026, United States:** ACPE updated its CPE Policies and Procedures Manual.
**10 April 2026, Australia:** the Pharmacy Board updated its CPD guidelines to remove outdated content on accreditation of CPD activities.

**15 May to 17 July 2026, Australia:** Ahpra and 14 National Boards, including Pharmacy, consulted on revised recency of practice and CPD standards; the draft proposes 20 hours a year including 5 interactive, with substantial notice before any change.
**20 November 2026, United States:** employers must update hazard communication programs and training for newly identified hazards in substances; the mixtures deadline is May 19, 2028.

blocks.title: Pending, not yet law
blocks.text: The HIPAA Security Rule proposal of January 6, 2025 would require security awareness training at least every 12 months and within 30 days of access for new members, but no final rule had been found as at the HIPAA page's last review. South Australia's Children and Young People (Safety) Act 2017 is to be repealed by a 2025 Act. Keep both as watch items.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each pharmacy obligation to its owner, its unit of measure and the learning outcome and assessment point it requires, so licensure topics and workplace duties sit in one structure without being confused. When a board changes a mandatory topic or a CPD standard, the affected roles are flagged. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Does the DEA MATE Act training apply to pharmacists?
faqs.a: The MATE Act applies to practitioners registered with the DEA to dispense controlled substances, other than those who are solely veterinarians, as a one-time total of 8 hours. The library's page frames it around prescribers, so a pharmacy should record it only for staff who hold a practitioner registration and confirm scope with the DEA.

faqs.q: Can in-house pharmacy training count toward Australian CPD?
faqs.a: Yes, in-house workplace CPD can count according to the Pharmacy Board's FAQ, but supervising interns is not CPD. Design internal sessions with clear learning outcomes and records so they can be claimed in the relevant group.

faqs.q: Do part-time pharmacists in Australia need fewer credits?
faqs.a: No. The Pharmacy Board allows no pro rata or part-time reduction, so a pharmacist working one day a week still needs 40 credits in the year to 30 September. The matrix should not reduce the target for fractional staff.

faqs.q: Who should track pharmacy technician training?
faqs.a: The library's pharmacist continuing education page does not cover technicians, who are subject to separate state rules. Give technicians their own rows, keep the workplace duties such as HIPAA and hazard communication, and add licensure columns once each state's rule is mapped.
